Julia Nguyen: noticed a bunch of customer errors on the embeddings endpoint around 10:03 PDT. Support tickets mentioning: 'Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024'. Seems tied to batched requests (batch_size 8+).
Samir Patel: saw the alert. 5xxs are fine, but 4xx errors spiked. Any recent runtime or routing changes?
Julia Nguyen: no app deploys, but runtime team pushed an update to batch coalescing heuristics at 09:50 that altered when different requests are combined.
Kevin Lee: could routing be grouping requests to a 1024-dim variant? Which model are customers hitting?
Jess (support): affected customer sample: uses hosted /v1/embeddings with model alias `text-embed-001` and client-side batching. Repro snippet attached. Error payload: 
```
HTTP 400: Embedding vector size mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024
 at /v1/embeddings
```
Rajiv Iyer: routing traces show some requests were routed to `text-embed-small-1024` under cost_aware policy because latency budgets were tight. The runtime then coalesced those into batches with requests intended for `text-embed-base-1536`. That causes the mismatch.
Samir Patel: can you paste an anonymized routing decision?
Rajiv Iyer: trace example: 
```
req=rz_0a7c
candidates=[text-embed-base-1536, text-embed-small-1024]
policy=cost_aware
selected=text-embed-small-1024
```
The issue: coalescer didn't validate embedding_dim before merging.
Kevin Lee: confirmed. Batched calls assume uniform vector size. The heuristic allowed coalescing across variants if seq lengths aligned, but forgot dimension compatibility.
Julia Nguyen: impact: partial degradation on embeddings route, error rate peaked ~17% for ~6-7 minutes. Multiple customers affected.
Jess (support): affected customer IDs: cust_1203, cust_888, cust_plat01. Some reported SDK retries that initially failed, then succeeded after a retry.
Samir Patel: short-term mitigation options: 1) flip runtime config to forbid cross-variant coalescing 2) add dimension check in coalescer 3) return explicit 422 when mixed-dimension batch detected so it doesn't hit the model. Who can flip the runtime flag now?
Rajiv Iyer: I can toggle on the control plane. Will set `batch.coalesce.allow_cross_variant=false` and restart the routing worker.
oncall-bot: config-change initiated by Rajiv Iyer (id=cfg-20260315-02)
Rajiv Iyer: flipped the config and bounced workers. Rolling metrics now.
Kevin Lee: I'll also add a safeguard: early check at the API layer to detect mixed-dimension batches and respond with helpful error text if seen. Lower risk than letting it reach model.
Jess (support): asked customer to retry their same payload. They retried and received 200s. Confirmed errors stopped.
Julia Nguyen: embedding 4xxs declined back to baseline within ~2 minutes of the flip. No new 'dimension mismatch' logs.
Rajiv Iyer: creating follow-up task for runtime: add explicit dimension compatibility gate in batch coalescer, unit tests, and safer canary rollout.
Samir Patel: action list: ENG-RUNTIME implement check and tests (P0), ENG-ML review routing cost_saver policy to avoid mixing variants, SUPPORT send RCAs and credits to impacted customers.
Kevin Lee: I'll draft a concise RCA doc. Root cause: batch coalescing heuristic combined requests routed to different embedding variants without verifying output dimension compatibility.
Jess (support): customers were offered mitigation (reduce client-side batch size or pin model). They appreciated the clear explanation and quick fix.
Julia Nguyen: resolving oncall incident. Logging follow-ups in backlog ticket RUNTIME-8732. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: please update docs to warn about mixing model variants in a single client batch and show how to pin model in SDK.
Kevin Lee: attaching routing traces and logs to the RCA.
oncall-bot: incident resolved (duration: 6m50s) by Rajiv Iyer
Julia Nguyen: marked resolved and created follow-up tasks in the runtime board.
Samir Patel: good catch, team.
